headline: Count-based, uncertainty-aware and sequence models link genetic variants to cell-type-specific expression
label: Donor Aware Genetic Effect Modeling
summary: New sc-eQTL, TWAS, and variant-scoring methods match genetic-effect models to donor and cell-type structure in expression and chromatin data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is fitting genetic-effect models to the donor- and cell-type-level structure of expression and chromatin data. jaxQTL uses negative binomial count models for pseudobulk sc-eQTL mapping and finds more eGenes than linear models, including distal ones. ATTICUS pairs personalised sequence representations with uncertainty-aware expression prediction, transferring bulk pretraining to cell-type TWAS. TriSCOPE applies donor-aware differential expression across ~4.2M nuclei from 627 donors to Alzheimer's disease programs. A second strand scores variants from sequence: ChromBPNet across 17 hematopoietic cell types scores 302,830 noncoding variants with lineage-structured effects complementary to GWAS, and Evo2VED provides Evo2 scores for 6.48M gnomAD variants. Other items (SPIN, SEMPER, scMINA, plasma protein panels) are adjacent applications rather than part of one pipeline.
